meaning: The number of men counted in the tribe of Simeon at the first census
description: The number 59,300 is the count of fighting men from the tribe of Simeon who were registered in the first census in the wilderness of Sinai (Num 1:23). The census included all men twenty years old and older who were able to go out to war. Under the leadership of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, the division of the tribe was placed in Reuben's camp on the south side of the tabernacle (Num 2:12–13). It is worth noting that Simeon's tribe experienced a dramatic decline at the second census, where the number fell to 22,200 (Num 26:14), representing the largest relative decrease among all the tribes. This decline is traditionally linked to the plague that followed the incident at Baal-peor (Num 25), in which a leader from the tribe of Simeon was directly involved.

footnotes.text: Simeon was Jacob's second son with Leah (Gen 29:33). The name means "he who hears" or "the Lord has heard," reflecting Leah's experience of being heard by God in her pain over being unloved.

In rabbinic tradition, the sharp decline of Simeon's tribe between the two censuses is linked to Zimri's sin at Baal-Peor (Num 25:14). The Talmud (Sanhedrin 106a) suggests that the 24,000 who died in the plague mainly belonged to the tribe of Simeon.

At the division of the land, Simeon's tribe did not receive a contiguous territory of its own but was given cities and villages within Judah's inheritance (Josh 19:1–9). This has been seen as a fulfillment of Jacob's prophecy in Gen 49:7, where Simeon and Levi were said to be scattered in Israel.
